title: Fat Albert
full_review:
"Hey, hey, hey! Don't throw your money away!"

"Fat Albert" (20th Century Fox) is a flat live-action comedy based on the characters of the long-running animated series (1972-79 and 1979-84) created by Bill Cosby, which itself was based on Cosby's stand-up monologues about growing up in Philadelphia.

Director Joel Zwick's big-screen version finds the heavyset hero (Kenan Thompson) and his colorful junkyard gang -- including Mushmouth (Jermaine Williams), Bucky (Alphonso McAuley) and Dumb Donald (Marques B. Houston) -- stepping out of their cartoon world and into the "real" world to help a troubled teen (Kyla Pratt) believe in herself.

Thompson -- with the help of a fat suit -- fills Fat Albert's trademark red sweater well enough, but his impersonation of the character's signature gravelly voice (supplied by Cosby in the original cartoon series) is inconsistent.

While imparting the same sort of positive life lessons, the family-friendly film lacks the intelligence, originality and fun of the groundbreaking Saturday morning show.

The movie's sole highlight comes at the end, when Cosby and his childhood buddies (on whom the junkyard gang is based) share a tender moment at the grave of the friend who was the inspiration for the character of Fat Albert.

This film contains brief crude language. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-II -- adults and adolescents. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG -- parental guidance suggested.
